leftEvidence.title: Chronicles retells victory, tribute, and administration

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Philistines, Moab, Hadadezer, Syria, Edom, and others are defeated; captured forces and dedicated objects are counted before the chapter names justice and officials.
points.right: David’s kindness is suspected, envoys are humiliated, Ammon hires chariots and Syrian forces, Joab divides the army, and a second Syrian defeat ends in submission.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places the retelling shares Samuel’s campaign outline while preserving different force numbers inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the parallel account preserves another set of numbers and troop categories inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Chronicles 18:1–17 and 1 Chronicles 19:1–19 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Succession, Retelling, and Temple Preparation” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Chronicles retells the Ammonite and Syrian war

payload.tension: 1 Chronicles 18:1–17 foregrounds the retelling shares Samuel’s campaign outline while preserving different force numbers; 1 Chronicles 19:1–19 foregrounds the parallel account preserves another set of numbers and troop categories. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
